statement: All elements of dates (except year) for dates directly related to an individual, including birth date, admission date, discharge date and date of death, and all ages over 89 and all elements of dates (including year) indicative of such age, are listed among the identifiers removed for safe-harbor de-identification; such ages and elements may be aggregated into a single category of age 90 or older (paragraph (b)(2)(i)(C)).
inference: Project inference: a birth date is a date element directly related to an individual, so a labeled birth date is a candidate pii value that gains the phi domain in a medical context. The year alone is outside the list, and an age under 90 is not listed. Applicability by holder is not settled.

notes: The list defines de-identification, not field semantics, and applies by holder.
Other admission, discharge and death dates are listed too but are not a birth-date kind; they are left to a future decision.

statement: Patient.birthDate is an optional (0..1) element of type date described as the date of birth for the individual.
inference: The element name and definition support a labeled-field role for birth dates in structured health records; the label vocabulary used by the cases (date of birth, DOB) is project-authored.

notes: Only the Patient element definition was read.
No label vocabulary for free text is source-stated.

statement: The FHIR date type is YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD with no time zone, and dates SHALL be valid dates.
inference: A year-only or year-month value is a reduced-precision date that FHIR admits; whether it still identifies is unsettled. Treating an impossible calendar date as not a valid date follows the source.

notes: The spec states validity for the date type, not for free-text fields.

statement: The full-date production is date-fullyear (4 digits) '-' date-month (01-12) '-' date-mday (01-28 to 31 depending on month and year).
location: RFC 3339 section 5.6, ABNF productions full-date, date-fullyear, date-month, date-mday
inference: The year-month-day order is fixed in this notation. Numeric forms with a different order or separator (for example day-first or month-first) are not covered by it, and the locale ambiguity of those forms is project inference, not source-stated.

notes: No source was read that documents locale-specific numeric date orders, so the day/month ambiguity case rests on inference.
